key_insight: Spatially evolving supersonic turbulent shear layers become self-similar downstream, and that similarity can be captured with new compressibility-aware scalings that also explain asymmetry and entrainment.
engineering_relevance: The results provide practical scaling laws and a closed-form entrainment relation for predicting mixing-layer growth and mass exchange in high-speed propulsion and aerothermodynamic systems.
method: Direct numerical simulations of spatially developing supersonic turbulent shear layers across multiple convective Mach numbers (Mc) and velocity parameters (λ).
Assessment of self-similarity using normalized mean velocity, Reynolds stress collapse, and linear growth of shear and momentum thickness.
Derivation of self-similar continuity, momentum, and energy equations plus an approximate cross-stream velocity and entrainment expression.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that profiles of turbulence quantities collapse in the self-similar region and that the approximate cross-stream velocity matches DNS results well.
watch_item: The proposed scalings and closed-form entrainment expression are validated in DNS, so applicability to different geometries, Reynolds numbers, or experimental flows may need additional verification.
paper_title: Numerical Study of Compressibility and Velocity Parameter Effects on Spatially Evolving Supersonic Turbulent Shear Layers
